papers.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
papers.summary: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass. papers.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
papers.summary: We propose LoopDVR, a framework for converting pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks. Rather than reducing the network width or depth directly, LoopDVR reuses Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and Transformer decoder, reducing the number of parameters while retaining the original computational structure. However, naively sharing parameters can disrupt the distinct transformations learned at different depths.

Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts.
